script: NBA players who every single college REJECTED, but still became LEGENDS! Coming out of high school, Steph Curry was six feet tall and weighed 160 pounds, and he wanted to play at Virginia Tech, where his dad, Dell Curry, is literally in their Hall of Fame. They watched him play and decided he wasn't good enough for a scholarship, so the most they offered him was a walk-on spot. Duke didn't even offer him that, and North Carolina's legendary coach, Roy Williams, later admitted he didn't remember seeing Curry during recruitment at all. And when he finally did see him, his only thought was, 'Man, he is little.' Not a single major Division One program in the country thought Steph Curry was worth the scholarship, but that rejection ended up being the best thing that ever happened to him. He signed with Davidson College, a tiny school in North Carolina with less than 2,000 students, and after just his freshman year, where he averaged over 21 points per game, all those big schools that passed on him started calling and begging him to transfer because Duke wanted him now and multiple major programs wanted him now. But Curry's response, according to his own father, was, 'They didn't want me then, and I don't want them now.' He stayed at Davidson, and in 2008, he led that team on one of the most electric NCAA tournament runs anyone had ever seen, taking them all the way to the Elite Eight while the entire country watched. He then got drafted seventh overall by the Golden State Warriors and went on to become the NBA's all-time three-point leader, a four-time champion, a two-time MVP, and the only player to ever win that award unanimously.
